headline: Broad Rally Caps the Week as Geopolitical Fault Lines Widen
body_html:
Friday's session closed on a decisively constructive note, with 413 of 549 names in our universe finishing higher and only 134 in the red — a three-to-one advance-decline ratio that underscores genuine buying breadth rather than a narrow-index illusion. Semiconductors led all sectors with a gain of 3.81%, followed by homebuilders at 2.62% and software at 2.32%. Energy was the lone sector in negative territory, slipping 0.58% as oil-services names weighed.

Single-stock fireworks were plentiful. Corsair Gaming surged 35.25% and Twilio jumped nearly 25% after what traders described as a pivotal week for cloud-communications sentiment. Natera climbed 21.37% on diagnostics enthusiasm, while semiconductor-equipment name Onto Innovation rose 14.74%, reinforcing the sector's top-of-table finish. On the other side, Trade Desk fell 21.9%, the steepest decline in the universe, as ad-technology spending outlooks remained in dispute.

Heading into the new week, the macro backdrop carries meaningful tail risk. Washington is monitoring a potential Strait of Hormuz agreement involving Iran and Oman, while a freshly announced mutual-defence pact among Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signals that regional fault lines are deepening. Senate confirmation of a wave of Trump administration nominees adds a domestic policy dimension worth tracking. Markets will need to weigh these geopolitical crosscurrents against what remains, for now, a broadly resilient equity tape.

briefs.headline: Celsius Holdings Surges on Stake-Building by Energy-Drink Entrepreneur
briefs.body: Celsius Holdings vaulted 16.83% on Friday after reports that the founder of Rockstar Energy has assembled a meaningful stake in the beverage maker and is seeking to install himself as chief executive. The news injected fresh strategic narrative into a name that had been range-bound, drawing momentum buyers into the close.

briefs.headline: Trade Desk Suffers Steepest Single-Session Drop in the Universe
briefs.body: Trade Desk plunged 21.9% on Friday, making it the week's most punishing decliner among tracked names. The ad-technology platform's results or outlook appeared to disappoint investors focused on digital-advertising budget trends, and the selloff reignited broader debate about ad-spend durability heading into the back half of 2026.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Tension Eases at the Margin as U.S. Flags Imminent Deal
briefs.body: A senior U.S. official signaled late in the week that a Strait of Hormuz arrangement between Iran and Oman could be reached shortly, offering a potential pressure-release valve for energy markets. Any confirmed agreement would matter acutely for crude flows, though ADNOC's warning that vessel and staff operations remain significantly disrupted suggests risks are far from resolved.

briefs.headline: Tripartite Defence Pact Reshapes Middle East Security Calculus
briefs.body: Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan announced a mutual-defence commitment as regional instability intensified, adding a formal military dimension to an already volatile landscape. The pact comes as Houthi forces struck Marib again and the United Nations cautioned that Yemen is edging toward a broader conflict, keeping energy and defence-adjacent equities on alert.

briefs.headline: Senate Confirms Wave of Trump Nominees, Reshaping Labour and Diplomatic Posts
briefs.body: The U.S. Senate confirmed dozens of Trump administration nominees across diplomatic and regulatory positions, including labour-board appointees that cement Republican influence over worker-relations policy. The rapid-fire confirmations narrow the administrative gaps that had left several agencies in acting-official limbo and could accelerate rulemaking relevant to financials and industrials.

briefs.headline: 'SaaSpocalypse' Debate Flares as Software Volatility Spikes
briefs.body: Wild intraday swings in software shares this week reignited an industry argument — dubbed the 'SaaSpocalypse' by some market participants — over whether artificial-intelligence tooling is structurally displacing legacy SaaS spending. The software sector still finished Friday up 2.32%, suggesting buyers are not yet capitulating, but the volatility flags elevated uncertainty heading into a fresh week of earnings commentary.
